clue.text: Vocal support for a physicist

indicators.note: something vocal is spoken, so the word for support is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a plank is a board that supports, as a shelf or a walkway does

explanation.surface: A request for someone to give a scientist a voice of encouragement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vocal support' reads as cheering on a scientist, but it is a board said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Planck was the German physicist who founded quantum theory.

clue.text: Father produced a cane for any complaint

definitions.note: an adjective phrase standing for a noun: a remedy that cures every ailment

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father

indicators.note: produced suggests the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: Dad brought out a stick to deal with any grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced' rearranges A CANE to ACEA.
explanation.definitionFit: A panacea is a supposed cure-all, a remedy for every illness.

clue.text: A coin found by idler becomes a collector's item

parts.note: L stands for pound, as in the old pound sign
a bum is an idle loafer

explanation.surface: A coin found by a layabout turns out to be valuable to collectors.
explanation.walkthrough: The collector's item is not the coin but the book in which stamps or photos are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: An album is a book for holding a collection of stamps, photographs or the like.

clue.text: Tiller girl?

parts.note: Tiller Girls were a famous British troupe of dancers; read literally it is a woman who works at a till

explanation.definitionFit: A cashier is the person who takes payment at a shop's till.

clue.text: Heartless teacher of religion in current language

indicators.note: the shortened teacher is placed inside the letters for current

parts.note: AC stands for alternating current

indicators.note: a heartless word loses its central letter, here the middle of the teacher's title

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher

explanation.surface: An unkind religious instructor teaching a modern tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' could be an insult to the teacher; it means only that the central B is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabic is the Semitic tongue spoken across North Africa and the Middle East.

clue.text: Memory, for example, of MacDonald

definitions.note: points to the first name belonging to MacDonald

parts.note: RAM is random-access computer memory
say is used to mean for example

explanation.surface: A recollection, for instance, of someone called MacDonald.
explanation.walkthrough: Ramsay MacDonald was Britain's first Labour Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramsay is the first name of the Labour Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald.

clue.text: Underwear at laundry can turn one's head

parts.note: a bra is an item of underwear
at a place means in it
the wash is the laundry

explanation.surface: Lingerie at the launderette could catch the eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' is a link; to turn someone's head here means to change their mind by indoctrination.
explanation.definitionFit: To brainwash is to alter someone's beliefs, figuratively turning their head.

clue.text: Drink stewed China tea, as they say

indicators.note: stewed tea is overbrewed and churned, so the letters are rearranged
as they say signals the next word is taken by its sound

parts.note: the word tea said aloud matches the sol-fa note ti

explanation.surface: Have some overbrewed tea from China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stewed' rearranges CHINA to CHIAN; 'as they say' turns 'tea' into TI by sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from Tuscany, a drink.

clue.text: Death rode softly in, providing material for the Guardian

indicators.note: the ride and the soft letter go inside the figure of death

parts.note: Death is personified as the Grim Reaper
to cycle is to ride a bicycle
p, piano, means softly in music

explanation.surface: The Grim Reaper pedalled quietly in, bringing stock for the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian, the paper that published this, used recycled newsprint.
explanation.definitionFit: Recycled paper is what the Guardian newspaper is printed on.

clue.text: Stud turns to sexual activity

indicators.note: turning a word round means its letters are read backwards

parts.note: bonk is British slang for having sex

explanation.surface: A stallion at stud heads off for some mating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stud' tempts as a breeding horse, but the definition is a knob as a raised boss or button.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a protruding boss on a surface, the same thing as a knob.

clue.text: Medium devised to dramatise love

indicators.note: something devised is worked out afresh, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, written as O

explanation.surface: A broadcasting medium was invented so that romance could be acted out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devised' rearranges DRAMATISE plus O.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam radio is a jocular old name for sound radio as a broadcasting medium, set against television.

clue.text: Something fishy to con the self-righteous

parts.note: a con is a swindle or scam
pi is British slang for sanctimonious, short for pious

explanation.surface: A suspicious scheme to trick the holier-than-thou.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something fishy' sounds like a racket but is literally a seafood dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are breaded langoustine tails, a seafood dish, so literally something fishy.

clue.text: Desire for youngsters to start in a job

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: someone in a job is earning a wage

explanation.surface: Young people's wish to begin working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to start' takes only the Y of 'youngsters'.
explanation.definitionFit: Yearning is an intense longing or desire for something.

clue.text: Girl bearing in a dish

indicators.note: the bearing is placed inside the girl's name

parts.note: Carole is a girl's name
SSE, south-south-east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A girl carrying something in on a plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing' looks like carrying but is a compass direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A casserole is a covered cooking pot and also the stew baked in it, a dish either way.

clue.text: Grammatical procedure of fictional felonious priest

parts.note: Dr Syn is the smuggling vicar in Russell Thorndike's novels
a tactic is a procedure or method

explanation.surface: A crooked clergyman's method in a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Syntactic means relating to syntax, the grammatical arrangement of words.

clue.text: Wise people need some imagination

indicators.note: some of the next word means a run of its letters is taken

explanation.surface: Being clever requires a bit of creativity.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside 'imagination'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magi were the wise men from the East in the nativity story.

clue.text: Anglican books of little value?

definitions.note: an adjective phrase pointing at a noun: a coin worth very little

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England, the Anglican church
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Church scriptures that are not worth much.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: a cent is the classic coin of tiny worth.
explanation.definitionFit: A cent is a hundredth of a dollar, a coin of minimal worth.

clue.text: Love ice cream without topping

indicators.note: without means outside, so the ice cream goes around the love

parts.note: a cornet is an ice cream cone
love is nil, written O

explanation.surface: Fancy an ice cream with no sauce on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without topping' reads as a plain ice cream, but 'without' is outside and 'topping' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronet is a small crown, something worn on top of the head.

clue.text: Perfect place for one to trade in

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a deal is a trade or bargain
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: An ideal spot for doing business.
explanation.walkthrough: IDEAL HOME is also the name of a long-running British exhibition of homes and household goods.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal home is a perfect place to live.

clue.text: Being clean involves giving it space

indicators.note: to involve is to wind up or entangle, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Hygiene means giving room to things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involves' rearranges IT and SPACE together; 'giving' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Aseptic means free from germs, sterile.

clue.text: Gruesome horse going round Hackney

indicators.note: the horse surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
a hackney carriage is a cab, the formal British term for a taxi

explanation.surface: A grisly horse circling the London borough of Hackney.
explanation.walkthrough: Hackney is a London borough, but here it is a hackney carriage, a cab.
explanation.definitionFit: Macabre means grim and gruesome, concerned with death.

clue.text: Leader once in a race over London green

parts.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
Lee Green is a district of south-east London

explanation.surface: A former head in a contest above a park in London.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places one piece above the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement Attlee was the Labour Prime Minister who led Britain after 1945.

clue.text: Headmistress comes in to make a treat for the afternoon

indicators.note: the head letter enters the word for make

parts.note: to make is to create
the head of the word mistress is its first letter M

explanation.surface: A school head arrives to prepare an afternoon snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Headmistress' looks like a school head but gives only M, which goes inside CREATE, followed by A.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream tea is scones with clotted cream and jam taken with tea in the afternoon, a British treat.

clue.text: Metropolitan to preach revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A city dweller sets out to preach about revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Metropolitan' suggests a city, but it is a church title.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Orthodox church an eparch is a bishop, and a metropolitan is a senior bishop of that rank.

clue.text: For assistance get a criminal for want of a better, as they say

annotationWithheld.why: For assistance get a criminal for want of a better, as they say (5): no parse found for AIDER; the homophone and 'for want of a better' cannot be matched to a criminal word
annotationWithheld.clue: For assistance get a criminal for want of a better, as they say

clue.text: One of a series this month on mental treatment

parts.note: inst., short for instant, means of this month in old business letters

indicators.note: treatment works the letters over into a new order

explanation.surface: An episode this month about psychiatric care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatment' rearranges MENTAL to ALMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An instalment is one part of a serial published in successive parts.

clue.text: Society girl takes time with what can reduce by 24s

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, is a young woman entering high society

explanation.surface: A debutante pays off by instalments over time.
explanation.walkthrough: '24s' points to the answer to 24 across: a debt is paid down in instalments.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt is an amount owed that can be paid off bit by bit.

clue.text: What a conscript wants is new kit etc

indicators.note: making something new reshapes it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recruit asks for fresh equipment and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new kit' looks like the conscript's wish; the ticket is the discharge papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ticket is old slang for a soldier's discharge, which a conscript longs to get.

clue.text: A blemish on the church is seldom found

parts.note: a scar is a mark or blemish
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A mark on a church is rare.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarce describes something in short supply, rarely seen.
